dedupe_keys.name: carilion clinic modelling situation awareness in intrahospital patient transport with discrete event and agent based simulation

description: This case study quantifies distributed situation awareness, how information about patients and tasks passes between staff, in intrahospital patient transport, and tests ways to fix communication gaps that lengthen stays. The authors, researchers at Virginia Tech, Carilion Clinic, King Saud University and Prince Sattam Bin Abdulaziz University, built a combined discrete event and agent-based simulation from a qualitative network of situation awareness transactions, observations and historical data, validated it with t-tests against transport times and patient counts, and published the work in an open-access journal article. Coverage is intrahospital transport at one health system. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives licence; the operational data are not public. Caveats: the model represents one service and site, and interventions were tested in simulation, not in practice. Across 1,500 replications, updating the charge nurse before picking up patients significantly reduced mean transport time and the cancellation rate, while updating the X-ray unit before arrival significantly increased transport time. Simulation uses: an example of adding communication and coordination to hospital patient flow models. Related records: the Bradford command centre study (case_study-bradford-royal-infirmary-hospital-command-centre) evaluates another coordination intervention.
